description: Friedrichs-vs-Krein selection survey: the S-map/LR fixed-point identity (F = S(K) exactly on the SW core), the ds/s harmonic-moment diagnostic along the nonnegative extension arc, the exact reason the modular criteria are orthogonal, and the moment-blindness of the whole arc

V1_smap_algebra.sw_jacobi_closed_form_matches_qd: exact, k ≤ 3 (α), k ≤ 2 (β), symbolic in v
V1_smap_algebra.sw_moment_S_fixed: v^{-k} G_{k+1}/G_1 = G_k exact for k ≤ 8
V1_smap_algebra.balanced_ratio_identity: m_{k+1}/m_k = q̃^k E (1 − p^{k+1}) exact, k ≤ 9
V1_smap_algebra.reading: the S-map (multiply by s, rescale by q̃) is J ↦ q̃^{-1}·LR(J); the SW core is an EXACT fixed point, the balanced family is not, and the whole obstruction is the Jackson factor (1 − p^{k+1}) → 1 geometrically

V2_F_equals_S_of_K_sw.statement: SW core: λ^K_j = q̃·λ^F_{j−1} and λ^K_j·w^K_j = w^F_{j−1} at every truncation order — the Friedrichs measure IS the s-multiplied, q̃-rescaled Krein measure (Christoffel/LR)
V2_F_equals_S_of_K_sw.consequence: the F/K choice is exactly the choice of s-power in the measure: ds versus s·ds.  It is the conjecture's own ς·ds/s normalization one level down, not an independent degree of freedom

V2b_balanced_smap_deviation.statement: balanced: LR(J)/q̃ ≠ J.  The Jacobi-data S-deviation decays at exactly p̃ = 1/q̃ (u1-promotion A-6), one square root off the moment-ratio rate p — S is an asymptotic, not exact, automorphism, and the obstruction is the Jackson factor

V3_harmonic_moment.sweep_parametrization_caveat: the sweep is LINEAR in the boundary shift t = s·t_N, in which I looks nearly flat until s → 1.  That flatness is a parametrization artifact: read the sweep against the invariant axis λ_min, which runs from λ_F down to 0.  The parametrization-free content is only (i) monotone, (ii) minimal at F, (iii) +∞ at K
V3_harmonic_moment.resolution_caveat: λ_min is ALSO nearly constant across the sweep and collapses only between s = 0.9999 and s = 1: at N = 44 the boundary-shift family does not resolve the INTERIOR of the extension circle at all, only its two endpoints.  The minimality of I at Friedrichs over the whole arc therefore rests on the operator ordering J_K ≤ J_t ≤ J_F (Krein–Ando), NOT on this sweep, which only corroborates it
V3_harmonic_moment.statement: I(μ) = (J^{-1})_{00} is the TOTAL MASS of the computational-time measure ν with μ = s·ν.  It is strictly monotone along the nonnegative-extension arc, minimal at Friedrichs, and exactly +∞ at Krein — the atom at s = 0 means no ν on (0,∞) satisfies s·ν = μ_K at all
V3_harmonic_moment.honest_caveat: Friedrichs-minimality of I is NOT independent evidence: J_K ≤ J_t ≤ J_F in the form order gives J_F^{-1} ≤ J_t^{-1}, so 'largest form', 'largest spectral gap' and 'smallest ds/s mass' are ONE fact in three costumes

V4_p3_orthogonality.sigma_squared_over_step_u_circle: 1  (moment shift is a lattice vector: blind)
V4_p3_orthogonality.sigma_squared_over_step_FK: 1/2 (moment shift is a HALF-lattice vector at odd k)
V4_p3_orthogonality.unexpected_finding: the Friedrichs masses are NEAR-proportional to the Gaussian samplings (spread ≈ 1.5, not orders of magnitude): exact proportionality is excluded, but the near-miss is the quantitative mechanism behind the parent audits' asymptotic u ≡ 1 alignment
V4_p3_orthogonality.statement: the KSel-3 dual-mode criteria (dual-positivity / modular inertness) are defined via the Poisson dual of a Gaussian sampled at step = variance.  The F/K supports have step 2L against variance L, and their masses (Nevanlinna masses 1/Σ p_n(x)²) are not Gaussian samplings at all — the criteria have NO domain of definition on the extension circle.  P3 is orthogonal, not merely inconclusive

V5_moment_blindness.contrast: every arc member reproduces every moment; the harmonic moment (V3) separates them, and separates Krein from the rest by ∞.  So the F/K ambiguity is invisible to the corpus's only current consumer class (integer moments)

V6_gamma_dry_run.prediction_tested: if μ_F ≈ e^{-s}ds truncated below its gap then I_F + ln λ_F → −γ as q → 1⁺, because ∫_λ^∞ e^{-s}ds/s = E₁(λ) = −γ − ln λ + O(λ)
V6_gamma_dry_run.outcome: REFUTED, scope-(a).  I_F + ln λ_F is N-STABLE to ~6 digits (the two badly pre-asymptotic legs cancel), so the ladder values 0.9802 / 0.9596 / 0.9506 and 0.9476 at the pins are converged in N — and they sit ~1.53 above −γ = −0.5772 and drift by only ~0.003 per major q step.  The truncated-exponential model is simply wrong for μ_F: I_F is ~2.6× E₁(λ_F), because μ_F is a q-LATTICE measure whose harmonic moment is dominated by the single lowest atom, not a truncated density.  Both readings are reported because they point opposite ways and the honest verdict needs both: the RATIO I_F/E₁ does fall toward 1 (2.52 → 2.06 → 1.78), so the leading behaviour is right, but the ADDITIVE residual I_F − E₁ GROWS (1.25 → 1.36 → 1.43).  The −γ test is an additive finite-part test, so it is the growing residual that governs, and the test as posed fails
V6_gamma_dry_run.non_discrimination: the mid-arc column agrees with the Friedrichs column to 7 digits at every rung — this quantity does NOT discriminate F from the arc interior; it separates Krein (where it is +∞) from everything else
V6_gamma_dry_run.unexplained_regularity_do_not_fit: I_F + ln λ_F sits near 0.95 across the whole studied q range and drifts slowly downward.  Recorded as an observation only.  It is NOT interpreted, NOT fitted, and NOT claimed to converge to anything
V6_gamma_dry_run.tier: EXPLORATORY — the q-ladder stops at q ≈ 1.2155 plus the pins; no claim is made about the q → 1 limit beyond the observed trend, which does not head toward −γ

summary.question: which self-adjoint extension of J(q) is distinguished — Friedrichs or Krein?
summary.P1_friedrichs_as_form: CONVENTIONAL-DEFAULT.  The polynomials are a form core of J_F by construction, but the SAME datum (operator + domain) determines J_K just as canonically.  The three 'independent' arguments for F (largest form, largest spectral gap, smallest ds/s mass) are one fact
summary.P2_krein_atom: EXCLUDES KREIN, DOES NOT SELECT FRIEDRICHS.  Exact core: μ = s·ν has a solution ν on (0,∞) iff μ({0}) = 0, which fails exactly at Krein.  Every other arc member passes
summary.P3_modular: ORTHOGONAL with a reason: the criteria are defined on a step-L sampled Gaussian; the F/K supports have step 2L and Nevanlinna masses.  No domain of definition
summary.P4_non_selection: LIVE.  No corpus consumer touches a non-moment functional of the kernel, and every arc member has every moment
summary.structural_finding: F = S(K) exactly (SW core, every truncation order): the F/K choice IS the ds-versus-s·ds level choice, i.e. the conjecture's own ς·ds/s normalization one level down
summary.no_fit: every scored item is an exact identity or a displayed-relation check
